name: W. F. Van Driesche
role: Medora postmaster; Stage company treasurer; Billings County treasurer, 1886
bio: William F. Van Driesche, who signed himself Wm. F. or W. F. Van Driesche, took a place in the Medora post office in February 1884 and signed the unclaimed-letter lists that March; he signed as assistant postmaster in the fall of 1884, and as postmaster from April 1885 through late 1886. In the spring of 1884 he signed the call for the Republican county convention and won a wager with Frank Keeler that he could ride a bucking horse for half an hour. He was treasurer of the Medora Stage and Forwarding Co., signing a March 1885 notice issued with the Marquis de Morès as president. In February 1885 he was elected president and treasurer of the new gun club, and in July 1885 he took the Marquis's place on a hunting trip to the Big Horn country with the Marquise. In April 1886 he was elected Billings County treasurer, and he also sat as an election judge; he was re-elected treasurer in November 1886 but resigned in December. In August 1886, when the prairie chicken season opened, he and Frank Foster bagged thirty-three birds in less than two hours.
